question: instruction cost of an automatic reclaim (shrink_to_fit on the JudyHS shim's two short-key tries every 65,536 JudyHSIns calls) under the owner's terms: every Callgrind arm within +0.1% of main with no allow-regression
instrument: replica of the CI Callgrind jobs: rust:1.100-trixie (rustc 1.100.0), Debian valgrind 3.24.0, iai-callgrind-runner 0.16.1, workspace bench profile (panic = unwind), EXPANSE_CDYLIB = that tree's release libexpanse.so; x86_64 (2x Xeon E5-2697 v4). Callgrind counts are deterministic; host load does not enter them

variants.a: process-wide AtomicU64 fetch_add in JudyHSIns; every 65,536th call sweeps both short-key tries before ins_slot
variants.a2: u32 countdown in the boxed ShortKeys, decremented by a shim-only ins_slot_reclaiming; at zero it resets and sweeps
variants.b: not built: no trigger without per-insert work was found outside alloc_raw_body!, whose edits measured negative in #1675, #1670 and #1095

sequencing: x86 first; AArch64 smoke and wasm fuel only for a shape that passes x86; neither shape passed, so they were not run
run_dependent_arms: judyhs_long_*_expanse* hash with a per-process RandomState; their base_rerun column is base's own spread
sweeps_in_ci_arms: 0: every judyhs_* arm inserts POP = 30,000 < 65,536 and runs in a fresh process; no other arm calls JudyHSIns

sweep_cost.instrument: callgrind --toggle-collect on an #[inline(never)] wrapper around ExpanseMap::shrink_to_fit, census key stream (mix32 addresses, seed 4242, 4 ports, 1,000,000-entry window), at 59119d217
